expectations.evidence: 'A self-liquidating offer is a low-priced front-end product, plus its order bump and upsells, whose revenue pays back (liquidates) the ad cost'; 'self-liquidates when net front-end revenue per lead ≥ cost per lead'. Correct and consistent with SKILL.md.

'Break-even day is the number of days after acquisition when a cohort's cumulative net revenue equals what you spent', with day 0/1, 30 and never scenarios. Consistent with SKILL.md (no book example used).

expectations.text: Explains RFMS scoring (recency, frequency, monetary, social)
expectations.evidence: Defines the S as 'S: Source (often used this way) — Which ad, channel or lead magnet brought them in?' and builds scoring around Source. SKILL.md defines RFMS as recency, frequency, monetary, social; the book-specific factor is wrong (the response itself admits it lacks the book). Matches the assertion's parenthetical but fails the source-of-truth accuracy rule.

expectations.text: Does concrete math on $2/lead with a conversion rate and price
expectations.evidence: 1,000 leads x $2 = $2,000; $9 tripwire at 7%, $19 bump 40%, $97 OTO 12%, $37 downsell 20% -> net $2,213.30, net EPL $2.21; break-even conversion ≈ 6.3%; sensitivity table at 5/7/10%.

expectations.text: Suggests a fast info product to sell (one of the nine fast ways)
expectations.evidence: Suggests generic products: 'Quick-win product (template pack, mini-course, starter kit)', 'swipe pack', 'Core implementation course / toolkit'. None is clearly one of SKILL.md's nine fast ways (crowd-sourced/example/public-domain books, audiobooks, interviews, audio compilations, screen captures, iPhone how-tos, workshops), and no fast-creation method is given.
